data.narrative:
Nimble Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company, was last valued at $1.0B post-money following $221M in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws on a peer set of four private companies at same or adjacent stages (Exotec at $2.0B Series D, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B Series B, Dexterity at $1.6B Series B, and Hadrian at $1.6B Series C), supplemented by one public comparable.

Two methods triangulate the current fair value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across the four-company robotics and manufacturing cohort also produces $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. Both methods converge on identical implied valuations, strengthening confidence in the result.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B, with a median of $1.7B. This represents a 70% uplift from the Series C post-money, consistent with stage-typical markups. Key uncertainty stems from the limited peer count and stage dispersion within the comparable set; valuation sensitivity to revenue growth trajectories and manufacturing automation adoption timing remains unquantified in available data.
